## Figure B1.4.1: Ukraine’s Long-Term External Debt Stock, by Creditor Type, 2015–25
Type: stacked area chart

- **Units:** US$ (billion)
- **Y-axis:** 0 to 250
- **X-axis:** 2015 to 2025
- **Series / legend:**
  - Private creditors
  - Multilateral creditors
  - Bilateral creditors
- **Country:** Ukraine
- **Time span:** 2015–25

### Approximate values by year
Values are estimated from the stacked areas and axis gridlines.

| Year | Private creditors | Multilateral creditors | Bilateral creditors | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈72 | ≈24 | ≈2 | ≈98 |
| 2016 | ≈69 | ≈24 | ≈2 | ≈95 |
| 2017 | ≈72 | ≈27 | ≈2 | ≈101 |
| 2018 | ≈74 | ≈25 | ≈2 | ≈101 |
| 2019 | ≈78 | ≈23 | ≈2 | ≈103 |
| 2020 | ≈81 | ≈27 | ≈2 | ≈110 |
| 2021 | ≈83 | ≈30 | ≈2 | ≈115 |
| 2022 | ≈80 | ≈43 | ≈4 | ≈127 |
| 2023 | ≈81 | ≈69 | ≈8 | ≈158 |
| 2024 | ≈74 | ≈94 | ≈9 | ≈177 |
| 2025 | ≈82 | ≈132 | ≈12 | ≈226 |

### Visual observations
- **Largest creditor type in 2015–2022:** Private creditors.
- **Largest creditor type in 2023–2025:** Multilateral creditors.
- **Smallest creditor type throughout:** Bilateral creditors.
- **Total long-term external debt stock** is fairly stable around **≈95–115 billion** from 2015 to 2021, then rises sharply after 2021 to **≈226 billion** in 2025.
- **Private creditor debt** stays relatively flat over the period, fluctuating around **≈70–83 billion**.
- **Multilateral creditor debt** shows the strongest growth, especially from **2022 onward**, rising from about **≈43 billion** in 2022 to **≈132 billion** in 2025.
- **Bilateral creditor debt** remains very small through 2021, then increases modestly from 2022 to 2025.
- **Highest total** occurs in **2025**.
- **Lowest total** occurs around **2016**.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
